correctness.rationale: In the static one-approved-candidate-per-voter party model with horizon ell=an, a whole party's unanimous coalition forces at least a b_j wins under PJR, EJR and EJR+; since these minima sum to ell, every fair outcome has x_j=a b_j. Conversely these counts satisfy all three axioms, yielding exact welfare a Q_n and price nM_n/Q_n. For iid uniform party labels, Q_n=n+2 times the number of coinciding voter pairs; coincidence indicators are pairwise independent, giving the required denominator concentration. Multinomial CLT yields the fixed-menu Gaussian maximum; occupancy maximum bounds yield log n/loglog n for linear menu; factorial moments of k-occupied bins give Poisson critical staircase and birthday cases, including eventual price one above n² labels. Independent exhaustive small profile checks confirmed exact integer quotas and welfare; classical occupancy proofs, not simulations, establish limits.
residual_risks: The theorem requires static exclusive approvals and integer ell/n, not arbitrary temporal utility profiles.
